construct: annual attributable health years lost, not exposure or rarity
interpolation: piecewise linear in log(1 + DALYs) between adjacent anchor points
policyExplanation: The decade-spaced middle thresholds are TULIP choices made before any current catalogue-score fit. A score around 9 represents health loss on the order of a major global cause in one year. The 10 ceiling is fixed to WHO's global 2021 all-cause DALY estimate. WHO did not endorse these score labels or thresholds.

points.meaning: No attributable annual health loss verified
About one hundred thousand full-health years lost worldwide in a year
About one million full-health years lost worldwide in a year
About ten million full-health years lost worldwide in a year
About one hundred million full-health years lost worldwide in a year, comparable in scale to one major global disease category
WHO's modeled global annual burden from all causes in 2021, used only as a fixed outer reference

boundaries: This is only a health-DALY component candidate; it cannot score service loss, broader welfare loss, ecosystem damage, or a whole dual-domain node.
The zero anchor means verified zero, not missing evidence.
Cause rows in the WHO workbook are comparison cases, not TULIP nodes, and their ranks or percentiles do not define the thresholds.
The 2021 all-cause ceiling and all thresholds stay fixed for this method version when new nodes are added; any revision requires a new method version and full recheck.
WHO source models have uncertainty. A WHO cause point estimate without an uncertainty interval is not a zero-width interval.
This candidate is not independently adjudicated and is not ready for publication.
